clue.text: Stony-faced companion's short and unusually shirty with me in study

parts.note: petro- is the Greek-derived prefix for stone, sitting at the face or front of a word

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so those letters are set out in a new order
something short has lost its end, so the abbreviation for companion is cut by a letter

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim-faced friend is curt and oddly irritable with the speaker during a study session.
explanation.walkthrough: PETRO + C (CH shortened) + an anagram of SHIRTY ME gives PETROCHEMISTRY. Shirty is British slang for bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrochemistry is a branch of chemical science dealing with petroleum, so it is a field of study.

clue.text: Carer's right: characters in shop aren't all eavesdropping

indicators.note: the answer is made of the letters sitting inside the following words, read straight through

parts.note: the run of letters starts at the end of shop and ends early in eavesdropping

explanation.surface: A shop worker insists they have rights, though not everyone in the store is listening in.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in aren't is ignored, as punctuation always is in a hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Parental leave is time off work a parent is entitled to, a right for someone caring for a child.

clue.text: Something toxic seen when peeling layers from lethal onion?

indicators.note: peeling strips the outer skins away, so each word loses its opening letters

parts.note: taken as written
Allium is the plant genus to which the onion belongs; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: A cook wonders what poison might be released by peeling a deadly onion.
explanation.walkthrough: Two letters come off the front of each word: LE from lethal and AL from allium, leaving THAL + LIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Thallium is a highly poisonous metallic element, once notorious as a rat poison and murder weapon.

clue.text: Bunch of stars addicted to drinking port

indicators.note: something drinking takes another thing into itself, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: to be on a drug is to be hooked on it
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A group of celebrities hooked on drinking port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the drink being consumed, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is a prominent constellation, a named grouping of stars in the sky.

clue.text: Dynasty that ruled empire in the past

definitions.text: Dynasty that ruled empire in the past

parts.note: the Han dynasty ruled the Chinese empire for four centuries
what is over is finished and past

explanation.surface: A royal house that once governed a great empire.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the House of Hanover, which ruled Britain and its empire from 1714 to 1901; read in parts, it is a Chinese dynasty followed by a word for finished.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hanoverians were the British royal house from George I to Victoria, ruling the empire at its height.

clue.text: Someone interfering with fruit tree called out

indicators.note: something called out is spoken, so the solver goes by how the word is heard

parts.note: the medlar is a small tree bearing brown fruit eaten when half-rotten

explanation.surface: A busybody tampering with an orchard tree gets shouted at.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddler is a busybody who involves themselves in other people's affairs uninvited.

clue.text: Agreeable writer's drawn into quarrel with name-dropping star

indicators.note: being drawn into something puts it inside, so the first piece sits within the quarrel

parts.note: a spat is a petty argument
the writer of the clue says I am, contracted

indicators.note: read literally, the star drops its abbreviation for name, losing one letter

parts.note: an icon is a celebrated figure

explanation.surface: A pleasant author gets dragged into a row with a celebrity who boasts of famous friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Name-dropping usually means boasting of famous acquaintances; here it removes N, the abbreviation for name, from ICON.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico, borrowed from Italian, describes someone congenial and likeable, easy to get along with.

clue.text: After a break, come back to answer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to return to a group or activity after being apart
second meaning: to reply, especially a defendant's legal reply

explanation.surface: Returning from an interval to respond to something.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to return to company left earlier and, as a legal term, to make a reply.

clue.text: Democratic leader recalled some secret sin: "I'm emir", perhaps?

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the letters are read from the far end
only some of the following letters are used, a run sitting inside the words

parts.note: the run starts inside secret and ends with the first letter of perhaps

explanation.surface: A leader of a democracy remembers a private confession of royal pretensions.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks and question mark mislead; the letters of secret sin I'm emir p, read backwards, give PRIME MINISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime minister heads the government in a parliamentary democracy such as Britain.

clue.text: Proper retreat soldier backed put in place again

parts.note: proper as in genuine

indicators.note: going backwards means the retreat and soldier are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier properly backed into retreat is redeployed.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign something is to bring it back into line, setting it in position once more.

clue.text: Fruit spread on the turn, if not rank

indicators.note: turning round sends the spread back the other way

parts.note: jam is a spread made of fruit
or offers the alternative, as if not does

explanation.surface: A jar of jam going off, if it isn't already rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: On the turn and rank both suggest food going bad; rank is actually a military grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Major is a military rank, above captain and below lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: Initially nervous youngster lays off newer material

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word that follows

parts.note: the heads of five words in a row

explanation.surface: An anxious young person lays off newer staff at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, a material used for stockings and clothing.

clue.text: Rude expression mugs rival off

indicators.note: something off is wrong or not right, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude remark sees off an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgarism is a coarse or offensive word or phrase, a rude expression.

clue.text: Ace newspaper putting colour back into pieces

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
The Sun is a British tabloid

indicators.note: putting the colour back means reading it in the opposite direction

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A first-rate newspaper restores colour to its torn-up pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means apart or in pieces, as in torn asunder.

clue.text: Private area perfect for Spooner?

parts.note: surface reading: the Reverend Spooner, whose name crosswords use for swapping word sounds
setter's reading: a spooner is someone who spoons, cuddling a partner, and the ideal private place for that is a bed for two

explanation.walkthrough: Spooner normally signals a spoonerism, so solvers hunt for swapped sounds; here it just means someone who likes to spoon, lying curled against a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed for two sleepers is the natural intimate spot for a couple to cuddle up together.

clue.text: Control animal that's kicking its hindquarters

indicators.note: kicking out the back end means the animal loses its rear part

parts.note: a reindeer is an Arctic deer

explanation.surface: Restrain a beast that is lashing out with its back legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The hindquarters are the whole second half of the animal's name, the word DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is a strap used to guide a horse, and to rein in is to restrain, so it means control.

clue.text: Meter reading conducted by gutless salesman is a con, sadly

indicators.note: being conducted by someone means being led along within their grasp, so one piece goes inside the other
without its insides, the word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters only

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gas meter reading done by a hollow salesman turns out, regrettably, to be a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: Meter reading suggests a utility visit; here meter is poetic rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Scansion is the analysis of a poem's rhythm, so it is a reading of its metre.

clue.text: See 8
War film that's hardly The Caine Mutiny

definitions.text: War film that's hardly The Caine Mutiny

parts.note: surface reading: the 1954 Humphrey Bogart film about a mutiny on a navy ship

parts.words: War film that's hardly The Caine Mutiny
parts.note: setter's reading: a 1964 war film starring Michael Caine, in which his soldiers stand firm rather than rebel

explanation.walkthrough: The Caine in the title belongs to a ship, but the clue points to Michael Caine's breakthrough film about the defence of Rorke's Drift in 1879, where the troops held their ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1964 film about the Anglo-Zulu War, with Michael Caine, is about loyal soldiers holding out, the opposite of a mutiny.

clue.text: Greek character's climbing tower, close to exhaustion

parts.note: climbing means going up
a silo is a tall storage tower

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A Greek hero is scaling a tower, nearly exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsilon is the twentieth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a Greek character.

clue.text: Brother performing with church beginning to improvise organ passages

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for brother
a performer is on stage
CH is the abbreviation for church

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A monk plays in church and starts improvising on the organ.
explanation.walkthrough: Organ passages suggests musical runs on a church organ; here the organ is the lungs.
explanation.definitionFit: The bronchi are the two main airways branching into the lungs, passages of a body organ.

clue.text: Rapid bot extremely confused, making for horrible user experience

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up and need sorting into order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A fast chatbot that goes haywire makes for a dreadful experience for app users.
explanation.walkthrough: User experience sounds like software design; the user here takes drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad trip is a frightening episode on a hallucinogen, a terrible experience for a drug taker.

clue.text: See 1
Spy chief regularly highlighted our so-called clout

indicators.note: in a down entry, being high means sitting on top, so the spy chief comes first

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: An intelligence boss often stressed what passes for our influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means power or influence, as clout does, as in political muscle.

clue.text: Drew Daliesque works

indicators.note: works suggests something being worked or manipulated into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist sketched surreal pieces in the style of Dali.
explanation.walkthrough: Drew looks like the past tense of drawing a picture; it is the sporting sense of tying.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that equalised levelled the score, and a match that ends level is drawn.

clue.text: Language from party putting off both sides

indicators.note: putting off both sides removes the letters at each edge

parts.note: a shindig is a lively party

explanation.surface: A tongue overheard at a party that turns off both factions.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is the main official language of India, spoken by hundreds of millions.

clue.text: Cackling individual feeding urge to laugh

indicators.note: feeding puts something into a mouth, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ha is a laugh
a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: Someone cackling keeps giving in to the urge to laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is famous for its cackling, laughter-like call, so it is a cackling creature.

clue.text: Terms of endless promise taking lead from Catch 22

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a vow is a solemn promise

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter
the answer at 22 is a word for clout, and an ab is an abdominal one

explanation.surface: The conditions of a broken promise seem drawn from Heller's novel Catch-22.
explanation.walkthrough: Catch-22 looks like the novel; it is split into Catch and a cross-reference to 22-down, MUSCLE, an example of which is AB.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocab, short for vocabulary, is the stock of words or terms a person knows.

clue.text: Criminal left another one to the auditor

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: another criminal, a fire-raiser

explanation.surface: One crook abandoned his accomplice to the accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditor suggests an accountant checking books; here it just means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A larcenist commits larceny, the crime of theft, so is a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Someone promising better service and reception when you sign new contract

definitions.text: Someone promising better service and reception when you sign new contract

parts.words: promising better service and reception when you sign new contract
parts.note: surface reading: a salesperson offering an upgraded phone deal with stronger signal

parts.words: Someone promising better service and reception
parts.note: setter's reading: a professional who organises a better church service and party when a couple marry

explanation.walkthrough: Service and reception sound like mobile coverage; they are the ceremony and party, and the new contract is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional organises a ceremony and its party for couples entering the marriage contract.
